definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta

reviewHistory.summary: Base disc rebuilt in board3d.ts from the spec (refine-code route). Three defects were found by looking at the comparison sheet and fixed in one correction round: a 64-tooth gear outline from per-vertex rim noise, a ring count that was half the real one because the radial profile aliased at a 4 px sample step, and a bark ring more than twice too thick. All four feature targets now clear their thresholds on agent vision. NOT CREDITED as a completed blockout pass: the gate requires an unlit map-stripped render as silhouette evidence and I did not capture one, so the pass stays open. Tier 1 silhouette IoU also FAILS at 0.794 and Divine Eye reports 0.40 / probe — both are measuring the CONDITIONAL reference (sky, trees and a hand fall inside the reference mask) and the declared team-token colour deviation, not the geometry.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: 32 of these render every frame under 32 skinned characters. One shared geometry, two shared materials, two 256px canvases. Nothing scales with piece count.

lightingFromPhoto: Key: direct low winter sun from the front-left, visible as the even bright wash across the face and the hard shadow on the hand. The game's existing DirectionalLight at (-4, 8, 5) is a fair match in direction; no light change is proposed.
Fill: open sky bounce, strong and blue. The game's HemisphereLight (0xdfe8ff / 0x33302c) already supplies this.
Rim / environment: none. The face is fully matte with no specular lobe at all, so envMapIntensity stays 0 and the material carries the look with roughness 0.92 alone.

Exposure and tone mapping: the reference is an outdoor phone frame with a clipped sky; the renderer keeps its current SRGBColorSpace output and no tone mapping, so the band field must not be pushed to match the photo's exposure.

Contact shadow / ambient occlusion: the disc sits flat on the board and already receives the shadow-mapped key light. Ambient occlusion is an independent low-frequency field from the band structure, strongest under the bark rim.

approximationNotes: STYLIZED, not matched. The reference is admitted CONDITIONAL: sky and trees behind it, a hand occluding the lower-left rim. Only the FACE is reconstructed; the slice's thickness is not observable in this view and is set by the game (0.06 units), not by the reference.

DECLARED DEVIATION: absolute colour comes from the project's team tokens (--team-light / --team-dark), which exist to say which side a piece belongs to. The reference contributes STRUCTURE (band radii, ring count, lobed perimeter) and RELATIONSHIPS (heart/sap luminance ratio 0.767) only.
Band contrast is deliberately held to about 12 percent around the team colour so a near-white base still reads white and a near-black base still reads black. Reference contrast is far higher.

The bark rim is mixed toward a MID brown, not toward black. Mixing toward a mid tone darkens the light team's rim and lightens the dark team's rim, so the rim reads on both. Mixing toward black would make it invisible on the dark team.
Bark PBR is DERIVED, not extracted: this photo has no bark-only region large enough or clean enough to sample. Heartwood (confidence 0.818) and sapwood (0.808) are extracted.

Detail 'matte-sawn-face' was first filed as kind 'gloss'. That was wrong: it describes the ABSENCE of gloss. Refiled as 'scratch' (the radial saw scoring); the matte claim is carried by roughness 0.92 and finishStyle.

componentTree was flattened during authoring: 'slice-body' was a duplicate of 'root' and the band components were filed as cylinders. A cylinder child is read as an appendage and demanded a positive embedDepth/overlap that does not exist here — the bands are painted regions on a flat face, not parts. Refiled as plane-card under root.
